page: Amazon Web Services r5n.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro system and engineered for network-intensive and memory-bound enterprise workloads. The underlying hardware utilizes an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs through hyperthreading. System memory comprises 512.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Networking throughput features a 75 Gbps baseline capability. The instance includes no local storage and contains zero GPUs, shifting storage requirements to attached network volumes.

Performance metrics reflect strong memory bandwidth and vector compute characteristics alongside moderate general execution. Uncached large-block memory tests show top-quartile throughput with 217.82 GB/sec for reads and 96.29 GB/sec for writes. PassMark database operations reached 21748.64 and extended instruction benchmarks scored 54153.69, highlighting efficiency in AVX-512 vector handling. Multi-core performance remains balanced, recording a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 61.0 GB/sec and a PassMark CPU score of 44219.0. In contrast, single-thread processing exhibits lower relative performance, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 1121.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 21.71 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration provides favorable resource density for workloads requiring vast RAM and low-latency node-to-node communication without local NVMe overhead. Given its memory capacity, 75 Gbps network interface, and 50.71 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, the r5n.16xlarge is architected for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, relational database servers, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r5n.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor for network-intensive workloads. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor delivering 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs clocked at 3.1 GHz. The configuration pairs 512.0 GB of DDR4 system memory with a 75 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no local storage and has zero GPUs. Benchmark results highlight strong uncached memory bandwidth at 217.82 GB/sec read and 96.29 GB/sec write, alongside strong PassMark database operations and AVX-512 extended instruction handling. Multi-core computational metrics remain competitive, though single-core throughput is modest across synthetic tests. With its combination of massive RAM capacity, high network throughput, and lack of onboard storage, r5n.16xlarge fits in-memory caching systems such as Redis, large distributed databases, and high-bandwidth data transformation pipelines.
